# ipterm

> ipterm (https://ipterm.net) looks up IP addresses, networks (ASNs), DNS records, a domain's email security (SPF, DMARC, DKIM) and its overall report card (DNSSEC, security headers, expiry), registry (whois) records and subnets. Every lookup has its own URL: browsers get a terminal-style page, and curl and scripts get JSON, plain text or aligned text. No API key, no sign-up, no cookies, and nothing about callers is stored.

Answers for the caller's own address come from Cloudflare's edge, so they describe whoever sends the request (the machine running your code), not the person you are talking to. Command-line clients (curl, wget, HTTPie, PowerShell) get JSON by default; other HTTP clients should add `?format=json` to be sure of JSON, or `?format=text` for aligned key/value lines. For an address or AS number the same works as a path, with no `?` for a shell to expand: `/8.8.8.8/text`, `/AS13335/text`, `/8.8.8.8/json`. `?color=1` adds ANSI colors to a text answer for people at a terminal; colors are never on by default, so leave it out when the output goes to a program. One-value endpoints return one line of plain text; a missing value is an empty line with HTTP 404. Uncached lookups are limited to 30 a minute per address (HTTP 429 with Retry-After past that).

IP address data powered by IPinfo (https://ipinfo.io). Networks: RIPEstat. Registry records: RDAP. DNS: Cloudflare's public resolver (1.1.1.1).

## Reference

- [Command-line help](https://ipterm.net/help): plain-text reference, the same as `curl ipterm.net/help`
- [OpenAPI description](https://ipterm.net/openapi.json): every route, parameter and response shape
- [API page](https://ipterm.net/api): the reference as a web page
- [Privacy policy](https://ipterm.net/privacy): what is and isn't collected

## Your own address

- [Your IP](https://ipterm.net/ip): the address as plain text (`curl ipterm.net` gives the same)
- [Your details](https://ipterm.net/json): IP, reverse DNS name, network, city, region, country, coordinates, time zone and Cloudflare data center as JSON
- One value each, as plain text: [/asn](https://ipterm.net/asn), [/org](https://ipterm.net/org), [/cc](https://ipterm.net/cc) (country code), [/city](https://ipterm.net/city), [/tz](https://ipterm.net/tz) (time zone), [/colo](https://ipterm.net/colo) (Cloudflare data center), [/hostname](https://ipterm.net/hostname) (reverse DNS)
- [Card](https://ipterm.net/me): `curl ipterm.net/me` draws IP, network, location, time zone and data center under a Braille world map, as text with ANSI colors for terminals. `?w=<columns>` (32 to 120) sets the width, `?color=0` drops the colors, `?redact` hides the IP. Meant for people at a terminal; use /json in code
- [One line](https://ipterm.net/line): IP, AS number, network name, country code and data center on one line (`203.0.113.4 AS64500 Example ISP · US · EWR`), for shell prompts and status bars
- [Expect](https://ipterm.net/expect/AS13335): `/expect/<AS number or country code>` (or several, comma-separated) answers HTTP 200 with the value when the caller's address matches and 412 when it doesn't, so `curl -fs ipterm.net/expect/AS13335 || <stop something>` works as a VPN kill switch. No outside call and no rate limit for any of these three

## Any address or network

- [IP lookup](https://ipterm.net/8.8.8.8): owner, network, location and VPN / proxy flags for any IPv4 or IPv6 address (`/<ip>`)
- [One value for an IP](https://ipterm.net/8.8.8.8/country): `/<ip>/<field>` with asn, org, cc, country, continent or hostname, as plain text
- [Network (ASN)](https://ipterm.net/AS13335): holder, registry, announced prefixes and main upstream networks (`/AS<number>`)
- [Routing](https://ipterm.net/route/1.1.1.0/24): how a public prefix or address is routed (BGP): the route that carries it, the network that announces it, RPKI validity, how many RIS peers see it and sample AS paths, from RIPEstat (`/route/<prefix>` or `/route/<ip>`)
- [As text](https://ipterm.net/8.8.8.8/text): `/<ip>/text` and `/AS<number>/text` give aligned key/value lines (`/json` for JSON); add `?format=text` to any other lookup for the same

## Tools

- [DNS](https://ipterm.net/dns/example.com): A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT and CAA records, the host of the first address and DNSSEC (`/dns/<name>`, or `/dns/<name>/<TYPE>` for one type with TTLs; an IP address gives its reverse DNS)
- [Mail check](https://ipterm.net/mail/gmail.com): a domain's email security, graded A to F: MX and the provider behind it, SPF (includes followed, DNS lookups counted against the limit of 10), DMARC policy and report addresses, DKIM keys at common selectors (add `?dkim=<selector>` for another), MTA-STS (record and policy file), TLS-RPT and BIMI. Each finding is ok, warn, fail or info, with a fix for every warn and fail (`/mail/<domain>`)
- [Domain report card](https://ipterm.net/grade/github.com): one A to F grade for a domain, with a fix for every problem (`/grade/<domain>`; a DNS record name such as `_dmarc.gmail.com` is a 400). DNS: DNSSEC, an AAAA record (IPv6), CAA (at the name or its closest parent) and an HTTPS record. Email: the mail check's grade (A ok, B warn, C or worse fail) and its main findings. Registration (RDAP): expiry (warn within 30 days, fail once expired) and the transfer lock. Website: one HEAD request to `https://<domain>/` (a GET, its body dropped unread, if the site refuses HEAD; redirects followed only within the domain) for HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection and Referrer-Policy, and one to `http://<domain>/` for the redirect to HTTPS; a 403, a bot challenge or a timeout counts as "couldn't check" (listed in `notChecked`), never as a fail. Grades: A no fail and no warn; B no fail, one to three warn; C one fail or four or more warn; D two fail; F three or more fail, an expired registration or broken DNSSEC. Certificates aren't checked
- [Badges](https://ipterm.net/badge/github.com.json): `/badge/<domain>.json` is the grade as a shields.io endpoint (`{"schemaVersion": 1, "label": "domain security", "message": "B", "color": "green", "cacheSeconds": 3600}`), for a README image `https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https%3A%2F%2Fipterm.net%2Fbadge%2F<domain>.json`, so readers' browsers never contact ipterm. `/badge/<domain>.svg` is the same badge drawn by ipterm, fetched from ipterm directly. Both cached for an hour
- [Whois](https://ipterm.net/whois/example.com): registry record for a domain, IP address or ASN over RDAP: registrar, dates, status, name servers, owner and abuse contact (`/whois/<query>`)
- [Subnet calculator](https://ipterm.net/cidr/10.0.0.0/22): network, broadcast, netmask, wildcard, usable hosts and how the block splits (`/cidr/<network>/<prefix>`, IPv4 and IPv6; the JSON makes no outside calls, and the page for a public range adds its routing)
- [Port check](https://ipterm.net/port/22): is a TCP port open on the caller's own address? `curl -4 ipterm.net/port/22` makes the server connect to the address the request comes from (never any other) and answers open, closed, no-answer or untestable (always for port 25, which Cloudflare blocks). Command-line clients only (browsers and search crawlers get a page explaining the port); 10 checks a minute. Like every "your own address" answer, it tests the machine running your code, not the person you are talking to
- [DNS leak test](https://ipterm.net/leaktest): which DNS resolvers look up names for the caller. In a browser, `leaktest` runs it with the other leak checks. From a shell, look up a random name first, then ask: `T=$(openssl rand -hex 10); dig +short $T.dl.ipterm.net; curl "ipterm.net/api/dnsleak?t=$T"` lists the resolvers that asked, with their networks (IPinfo Lite), once. Tokens are 20 lowercase hex characters; the names answer NXDOMAIN on purpose
- [Shared leak test result](https://ipterm.net/leaktest/r/1bjp): `/leaktest/r/<code>` is the link `share` gives after the leak test in a browser. It answers with the result decoded from the code alone, `{"code", "grade", "vpn", "checks": {"dns", "webrtc", "ipv6", "tz"}}` as JSON (`?format=text` for aligned lines): grade A to F, `vpn` "a VPN was on", "no VPN detected" or "couldn't tell whether a VPN was on", and each check "no leak", "leaked" or "not tested". The code holds nothing else (no IP address, provider, location or resolver), so nothing is looked up or tested; an invalid code is a 404 with `{"error"}`
- [Search](https://ipterm.net/go?q=8.8.8.8): `/go?q=<anything>` redirects (302) to the page for an IP address, AS number, domain or URL, range, email address (its mail check) or `port <n>`, or for a terminal command such as `dig gmail.com MX` or `grade github.com`. Browsers use it to add ipterm as a search engine ([OpenSearch](https://ipterm.net/opensearch.xml)); with curl, add `-L`

## Optional

- [Guides](https://ipterm.net/guides): private IP ranges, finding a router's address, what an IP address reveals, IPv4 vs IPv6, ASNs, subnet masks
